About the Position

Two fully funded PhD positions are available exploring what happens when textbook assumptions about near-field waves are removed.

OpportunityFully Funded PhD Studentship: Near-Field Wave Physics (ERC ATLANTIS Project)
HostKing's College London
LocationLondon, United Kingdom
Study LevelPhD
FundingFully Funded
StipendMaintenance stipend + tuition fees + additional research
Application Deadline1 November 2026, 00:00 GMT
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

Funding detail: Maintenance stipend + tuition fees + additional research funding

Basic Information

  • Full Project Title: Near-Field Wave Physics (ERC ATLANTIS Project)
  • Host Institution: King's College London
  • Department: Physics / Engineering
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Duration: 3.5 years
  • Start Date: 2026/27
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded
  • Stipend: Maintenance stipend + tuition fees
  • Additional Funding: Conference/workshop attendance, training, collaboration visits, publication costs, research software
  • Eligibility: Open to all nationalities
  • Application Deadline: Open (as of late July 2026)

Project Overview & Significance

This is a rare opportunity to engage in fundamental wave physics research funded by the European Research Council (ERC) under the ATLANTIS project. Hosted by the Department of Physics and Engineering at King's College London, this project pushes the boundaries of conventional physics. It challenges the standard textbook assumptions about near-field waves. Near-field physics is crucial for advancements in metamaterials, advanced sensing, and high-resolution imaging. By removing traditional assumptions, the research aims to uncover new physical phenomena and methodologies that could revolutionise how we manipulate and understand wave-matter interactions at the nanoscale.

Research Themes & Objectives

The successful candidates will investigate the fundamental limits and behaviours of near-field waves in complex media. The research will likely involve theoretical modelling, computational simulations, and potentially experimental validation. Key areas of interest include the engineering of metamaterials with exotic properties, the development of super-resolution sensing technologies, and novel imaging techniques that surpass the diffraction limit. The project is inherently fundamental, meaning it seeks to answer deep physical questions that have broad downstream applications in telecommunications, medical imaging, and materials science.

Training & Development

Funded by the ERC ATLANTIS project, these PhD positions come with exceptional financial support that goes far beyond a standard stipend. Students will have dedicated funding for conference and workshop attendance, allowing them to present their findings to the international scientific community. Additional funding covers training activities, international collaboration and dissemination visits, publication costs in high-impact journals, and access to specialised research software. Candidates will be trained in advanced computational techniques, theoretical physics, and research methodologies, positioning them for leading roles in academia or high-tech industries.

Eligibility and Requirements

Applicants must hold a minimum of an undergraduate degree with a 2:1 honours in physics, engineering, or a closely related subject. A strong background in electromagnetism, wave theory, or computational physics is highly desirable. Given the fundamental nature of the research, candidates should demonstrate a deep curiosity, strong analytical skills, and the ability to tackle complex, abstract problems.

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Official Link

Full announcement and application portal: https://www.kcl.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-research/areas/physics-research-mphil-phd

Source: kcl.ac.uk - the details in this listing were recorded from this official page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 1 November 2026, 00:00 GMT - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

About King's College London

King's College London is a public research university and a Russell Group member. Its undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes span medicine, law, humanities, psychology, science and other disciplines. With campuses across central London, King's connects academic study and research with healthcare institutions, cultural organisations and wider questions affecting contemporary society.

Official website: https://www.kcl.ac.uk/

How to Apply

Prospective candidates should apply via the relevant Physics or Engineering PhD programme at King's College London. It is recommended to check the "Fully Funded PhD for International Students" listing on FindAPhD for exact project details and to contact the prospective supervisor directly to discuss research alignment prior to applying. Please quote '1029' when applying as the funding code/reference.
